title: Cap. VI Arg. 13 close: two impieties — explode foresight election; good use is benefit, not mover
pass_a_gloss: To finish in a word: Since this opinion of the election of singular persons to life from their foresighted faith involves these two things most hostile to grace, namely, that the first love of God by which he destines singular persons to life arises from the good use of free choice prevented by grace, and that faith itself is not infused into certain persons from a special gift, but is conceived in certain persons from a special good act of free choice, it is to be exploded by all the orthodox; and on the contrary it is to be established that the good use of grace foreknown by God was not the cause which moved God to elect these before others, but was rather a special benefit of election.
pass_b_english: In a word: this view — electing singular persons to life from their foresighted faith — involves two things most hostile to grace: that God's first love destining them to life arises from the good use of grace-prevented free choice; and that faith itself is not infused into certain persons by a special gift, but conceived in them by a special good act of free choice. All the orthodox must explode it. On the contrary: the good use of grace God foreknew was not the cause that moved him to elect these before others — it was rather a special benefit of election.
source_text: Ut verbo absolvam: Quandoquidem haec opinio de electione singularium personarum ad vitam ex praevisa fide eorundem involvit haec duo maxime gratiae inimica, nempe, Primum Dei amorem quo ad vitam destinat singulares personas oriri ex bono usu liberi arbitrii per gratiam praeventi, et ipsam fidem non certis personis ex speciali dono infundi, sed ex speciali bono actu liberi arbitrii in certis personis concipi, ab omnibus orthodoxis explodenda est; et e contra statuendum, bonum usum gratiae a Deo praescitum non fuisse causam quae Deum movebat ut hos prae aliis eligeret, sed fuisse potius speciale beneficium electionis.
